subject.title: fix: block no-auth managed gateway LAN installs

question: Should this PR intentionally make explicit no-auth non-loopback managed Gateway installs fail at install/refresh time instead of only failing later at Gateway startup?
rationale: The code matches the existing runtime security boundary, but it changes the timing and user-facing failure mode for existing invalid managed-service configurations.

options.title: Accept the earlier install block
options.body: Merge the preflight as the clearer failure mode for an auth/bind configuration that current runtime already refuses.

options.title: Ask for fuller managed-service proof
options.body: Require a redacted Windows Scheduled Task or equivalent managed-service refresh transcript before accepting the compatibility change.

options.title: Pause for the broader update claim
options.body: Leave the PR open until someone proves whether the updater itself writes gateway.bind=lan from an omitted field.

recommendation.title: Accept the earlier install block
recommendation.body: Merge the preflight as the clearer failure mode for an auth/bind configuration that current runtime already refuses.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle is the strongest history signal for Gateway startup/auth hardening and managed-service install behavior.
